lanesKeeper.text: All three, and no coin for any of them. King Might had them laid the year the gates woke — said a city that only knows how to fight forgets how to be a city.
Shoes are on the rack behind me. Take a pair, bring them back, that is the whole arrangement.
Two boards on the north wall, and they are properly weighted — not like the tavern's, which lean left and always have.
And the jukebox by the east wall. Put something on. The quiet in here gets loud.
ROOK at the table bowls a hundred and forty-seven, near enough every week, and I have watched him do it for two years. Never a word about it either.
Gale down at lane one has been trying to beat him since the spring. Ask him how it is going. Go on.
And NERA at the racks holds the house — two hundred and twelve. She will tell you it was luck. It was not.

lanesRegular.text: Do not. Mott sent you over to ask that, and he does it to everyone.
Forty-one weeks against ROOK. Forty-one. I have beaten him on the first ball, on the fifth frame, on the ninth — and never once at the end of it.
Nothing! That is the horror of it. Same line, same speed, same little nod before he lets go. No spin, no risk, no flair.
I throw a beautiful ball. Absolutely beautiful. And then I throw a gutter, and he throws his hundred and forty-seventh pin, and we go home.
Start left of centre and let it drift in. And do not chase a strike on the second ball — a spare counts, and a gutter counts for nothing.
Advice I give freely and have never once taken.

lanesRecord.text: You are the one with the record?
Two hundred and twelve. Four years ago, lane two, a Tuesday, nobody in but Mott and a fox who left at the sixth frame.
I have not come within thirty of it since. I do not mind. It happened.
No. Rook bowls against the pins and Gale bowls against Rook, and neither of them is having any fun at all.
I come down, pick a ball, throw it badly, and go home. That is the whole sport.
Every chance. It is a good number, not a great one — the great ones are up near three hundred and I am not built for those.
Go on. I would rather lose it to somebody than sit on it another four years.

lanesRival.text: Eleven years. Same table, same ball, same fourteen pounds of it. I had it drilled before the lanes were re-laid and I have not seen a reason to change.
A lane asks you the same question ten times and does not care what you did yesterday. There is not much else you can say that about.
Gale says you bowl the same score every time.
A hundred and forty-seven. Occasionally a hundred and forty-four, and once — once — a hundred and fifty-one, which unsettled me for a month.
He throws for three hundred every single frame. It is magnificent to watch and he has not beaten me once in forty-one.
Nera has the house and she is welcome to it. Chasing a number is how Gale ended up like Gale.
I want a hundred and forty-seven. I get a hundred and forty-seven. Try the middle lane — it runs true.
